exercise.name: Cable Lying Single Arm Cross Lateral Raise

reference.title: Cable Lying Single Arm Cross Lateral Raise
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching: lying face up, the arm or arms sweeping out from the hips to shoulder level against crossed low-to-mid cables)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you raise, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen; light: the arm is a long lever
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; slower lowering

cues.text: Lie face up on a flat bench, feet flat, with cable towers beyond your feet. Hold the handle from the tower on your left in the right hand, so the cable crosses over your legs; left arm relaxed at your side, hands beside the hips, elbows soft.
Breathe out and sweep the right arm out to the side along the bench, elbow soft, until the arm is level with the shoulder.
Arm out at shoulder level, shoulder blade on the bench, ribs down.
Breathe in and bring the hand back toward the hip slowly; do not let the cable pull it in.
Brief pause with the cable taut, then repeat; switch arms after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the shoulder blade off the bench to reach
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper back flat on the pad; shorten the range.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbow more as the arm moves out
mistakes.fix: Keep the same soft elbow through the sweep.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the cable snap the arm back

kinematics.norm: From beside the hips to about 90 degrees (the range used by Coratella 2020 for the dumbbell raise)
Elbow soft, about 10-20 degrees, held nearly constant (clinical opinion)
Lying face up removes most of the gravity load on the sideways sweep, so the crossed cable supplies the resistance and keeps it on at the start (clinical opinion)
Head, upper back and hips on the pad, feet flat (clinical opinion)
About 2 s out, a short pause, 2 s back (clinical opinion; Coratella 2020 used 2-0.5-2 with dumbbells)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Lying Single Arm Cross Lateral Raise, video (movement reference)
Coratella et al. 2020, an electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(17):6015)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: start light; the arm is a long lever.
Get the handles before lying down and hand them back (or let them return slowly) before sitting up.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Pinching near shoulder level: stop at about 70 degrees.
Lower-back discomfort: put the feet on the bench end.

muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Prime mover: sweeps the arm out against the cable. The lateral raise gave the highest medial deltoid activity among the tested exercises (Campos 2020, dumbbells).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Helps the sweep, more if the arm drifts toward the ceiling.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade as the arm moves out.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Supports the shoulder blade; reaching or shrugging shifts work here.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still on the bench.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the cable's pull to turn the trunk.

guides.label: Hand sweeps out along the bench
